what: Every call on ATOM's serving path that can stop a thread, and what a simulated run has to do about it. Rows under 'sites' are produced by the scanner in sync_scan.py and classified by hand; rows under 'anchors' are points that are not a call -- a loop gate, a stamp, a compiled-in bound -- and are pinned to a piece of text that occurs once in the symbol they name instead.

categories.A: simulated time decides this, not the real clock: a duration that is predicted rather than elapsed, a reading the result reports, or an idle loop that must jump to the next event
categories.B: parks until another process sends something, with no bound; the call stays as it is and the process says when it is idle
categories.C1: a bound that exists to declare something broken; raise it or switch it off
categories.C2: a bound that sets a cadence; keep the cadence on simulated time and poll briefly for real so the thread stays responsive
categories.ignore: invisible to the simulated result: inside one process, at startup, at shutdown, below the replaced forward pass, or in a backend the simulator substitutes
categories.undecided: the reading depends on a decision that has not been made

boundary: A bounded wait for another process is C1 or C2 by what the bound is for; the same wait without a bound is B. A wait whose peer is a thread of the same process is ignored, because the process is not idle while one of its own threads is parked.

mechanisms.K1: event cost: the clock owner advances the LP's clock by a duration the cost model or a resource station prices
mechanisms.K2: clock read: returns the LP's logical time
mechanisms.K3: idle point: the clock owner waits for the LP's next event rather than spinning or parking on the real clock
mechanisms.K4: channel send: stamped with the LP's time and logged on the clock owner
mechanisms.K5: channel receive: counted at the wait point, and delivered in timestamp order once the LP's clock passes its arrival time
mechanisms.K6: wait inside one LP: never reported to the clock authority; its duration belongs to the event the clock owner is pricing
mechanisms.K7: virtual timer: the bound runs on the LP clock
mechanisms.K8: real bound: the clock authority cannot reach it, or it stays real on purpose; it is configured rather than simulated
mechanisms.K9: outside the model: outside the simulated window, inside code the simulator replaces, or cannot park

history: category and why are the first classification, kept as written; rows added since carry none. mechanism and mechanism_why are what a simulated run does at the site: mechanism_why is empty only where the mechanism is the one the row's category named (A K1, B K5, C1 K8, C2 K7, ignore K9) and why already says it.
